newsitem.title: USA: Kohl meets Clinton in visit to mark Marshall Plan.
newsitem.headline: Kohl meets Clinton in visit to mark Marshall Plan.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and President Bill Clinton met on Wednesday for a working dinner to discuss the European Union, the G7 summit in Denver this month and to renew their friendship.
Kohl arrived in Washington earlier on Wednesday for ceremonies marking the 50th anniversary of the Marshall Plan.
The two men met for a private dinner at an exclusive Italian restaurant in historic Georgetown district, where they dined in a private room.
Clinton underscored the importance of the U.S-German relationship in brief remarks to reporters before entering the restaurant.

Asked about the subject of their dinner, Kohl said they would discuss the state of the European Union, preparations for the July summit in Denver of the Group of Seven industrialised nations, the upcoming U.N. General Assembly and "renewing our friendship."
Clinton's National Security Advisor Samuel Berger and his German counterpart Joachim Bitterlich also attended the dinner.
Kohl was due to attend a wreath-laying on Thursday morning and go to an evening gala to commemorate the work of former Secretary of State George Marshall.
Under the Marshall plan, which he briefly outlined in a speech at Harvard University on June 5, 1947, the United States provided billions of dollars in aid to rebuild Europe after World War Two.
